focus.jnote: The environment is calmer than Tuesday but still two-sided. The U.S. and Iran remain in an active exchange around the Strait of Hormuz — Washington launched fresh strikes on Iranian targets this week and threatened more devastating attacks, while Iran retaliated with drones and missiles at U.S. bases; Trump said the latest attacks would be short-lived but signaled readiness for more. Crude eased slightly but held above ~$90 WTI (Brent ~$95) as shipments continued to move through Hormuz — roughly a fifth of the world’s oil passes through it. The surge fed inflation fear that drove the 10-year yield to ~4.81%, its highest since 2023, and markets now price ~two-thirds odds of a September Fed hike after Chair Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole remarks. ADP came in soft (+38k, weakest since January) and Friday’s NFP is the marquee event. The VIX has cooled toward ~16 and gold pushed back above $4,400. This is a live conflict layered on a hawkish-Fed, jobs-week tape — not a premium-selling backdrop.
focus.notdown: Energy / oil-refiners (CRAK, XLE, XOM, MPC) are the group catching a supply-fear bid — CRAK printed a fresh 52-week high near $62.75. But this is a two-sided war trade: one de-escalation or Hormuz-reopening headline gaps crude back down and takes energy with it. Note refiners are ambiguous beneficiaries — crude is their input cost, so a spike can pinch margins even as the ETF rides the theme. Watch, size small.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive growth and high-beta tech are pressured by the 20-month-high 10Y, and even a blowout like HPE (record EPS, raised guidance) gapped DOWN ~5% on margin and memory-supply worries. But selling bear calls into a headline-driven, hike-fear, pre-NFP tape carries violent squeeze risk on any peace or dovish surprise — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today and confirm liquidity before touching anything.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite 68 is deep in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 42% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an active military exchange with an oil shock, a ~20-month-high 10Y, a live September rate-hike debate, and NFP Friday stack an unscheduled tail on top of a scheduled one — you cannot time or size around either. The scanner boarded two names, but both carry hard gates (CRAK’s next-earnings/roll gate is UNKNOWN and it’s a refiner where oil is an input cost; HPE’s liquidity is UNVERIFIED, OI is thin at 66, and its volume read was near zero). Stand down on new credit spreads. Cash is a position today.
